correctness.rationale: Discrete Fourier inversion establishes the two-level constants exactly. The sine-log identity reduces magnitude flatness to zero-character transforms. For every nonprincipal even character of the unit group, use its primitive conductor, a Gauss-sum identity and nonvanishing L(1,chi) to force a vanishing Fourier coefficient of signed multiplicity difference. Principal coefficient vanishes by permutation; quotient character orthogonality yields signed 2-invariance. Conversely that invariance kills all sine-log sums. Finite standard-library checks corroborate, not replace, these arguments.

originality.rationale: Gaitanas 2023 proves signed doubling progression structure for uniform nonempty subset sums under restrictions, whereas this theorem gives an exact if-and-only-if for two-level autocorrelation for any odd modulus, including nonuniform cases. Ciprietti–Glaudo Section 4 studies fiber equality and, for its structural conclusion, Proposition 4.6 assumes special moduli. No inspected statement implies the complete all-odd Fourier-magnitude equivalence; the classical Dirichlet-character nonvanishing is an input. Searches did not find a dominating statement; unindexed equivalence is a residual risk.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact classification of a two-level subset-sum autocorrelation invariant across every odd modulus. It supplies a structural all-moduli Fourier test and a distinct nonuniform modulus-nine boundary, addressing the mathematical gap between uniform subset sums and signed doubling generators in Gaitanas’s research. It is not a mere isolated enumeration or trivial reformulation of a known table.
